content.comment_body: Apologies for adding to this topic. I'm also having trouble. I can see the [product_name] on the PC connection screen and when I try to test the connection, it takes some time before an error appears. I have two [product_name] devices on a network; one connects and transfers data as expected, but the other is only visible and doesn't connect. I tried resetting it to factory settings and connecting it directly to the PC, but there's still no connection. Might there be a faulty link in my network program that caused this? Should a reset solve the problem?

Hello [user_name], welcome to the forum. There isn't enough information to diagnose the issue. Which [product_name] models are you using exactly? Please provide the specific [article_no] and firmware details. Also, specify which software version you're running. Is the device that's not connecting a new unit?

Thanks for your quick reply. The device is new, [article_no] (the old one is [article_no]). The firmware version on the new device is [version_no], and the older [product_name] is running [version_no]. I'm currently using [product_name] [version_no].

That's likely the issue. You have a new [product_name] and it requires [product_name] [version_no]. You can get the upgrade online, but downloading this software might have export restrictions and require special registration. Why is login and additional data needed for export-restricted downloads?
Thanks, I'll download the new software now. I thought the issue was on my end. I'll take a break for now and hope to get the updated software soon.

I finally had the chance to try out the new software. Both the new and older [product_name] devices now work on the network and I can program and monitor them. Next, I want to connect them over a WAN so they can communicate with each other. Is this possible? I have two identical 4G routers with data plans, and I would like to set up the connection over the internet. Despite several attempts—including disabling the firewalls, forwarding port 10001 as suggested in the forum, and using the public IPs from Myip—I haven't been able to establish communication over WAN. The LAN addresses for both routers are 192.168.8.1, with the [product_name] devices at 192.168.8.3 and 192.168.8.4. The public IP addresses for the routers are anonymized. Which IP should I use in my program to enable communication over the internet? For testing, I tried connecting the [product_name] devices over a power supply cable using two communication sockets (no internet involved) and they were able to communicate successfully. Would appreciate help to configure the internet setup for remote communication. Apologies for my English—I'm from the Netherlands.

analysis.insight_summary: The user struggled with connecting a new [product_name] module to a PC via network, despite the device being visible in the software. The problem was identified as a mismatch between hardware and software versions, requiring an upgrade to the newer programming software. After updating, both devices operated correctly on the local network. The user then attempted to configure WAN communication using 4G routers, but faced persistent issues despite following common networking troubleshooting steps, highlighting the challenge of establishing reliable remote connectivity for these devices.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects a straightforward setup for both local and remote programming, monitoring, and communication of their [product_name] devices, hoping that commercially available networking hardware can provide reliable connectivity over the internet.
